text:
Tara (PM): team — quick final pass on the partner pilot contract and scope. We need clear rules for scope negotiation (what we promise to deliver), how we handle partner-requested feature work vs bug triage, and the acceptance criteria we put in the invite. Goal: send invites at 09:00 PT tomorrow.

Ethan (Eng): can we separate two tracks: "operational support" (bug triage, config help) vs "product changes" (feature asks). Ops = included in pilot; Product changes = separate change request with prioritization and timeline expectations.

Zoe (CS): +1. For ops, propose a weekly ops cap per partner: 3 hours/week for deep partners, 1 hour/week for light. Anything beyond should be logged and billed as engineering change requests.

Felipe (Design): from partner burden POV, we must specify what counts as "feedback". Offer two channels: short structured form (3 questions) and optional 30m recorded session. Make the form required for milestone progression.

Rina (Legal): simplest approach: a 1-paragraph pilot addendum that covers telemetry, IP for feedback, and a 30-day rollback notice. Keep it standard and attachable to existing MSA. Avoid custom clauses unless customer is enterprise.

Tara (PM): draft rules I'm proposing:
- Slot types: 6 deep / 6 light (12 total)
- Deep = expected 3h/week, priority ops (24h triage for P1), telemetry opt-in, one KV-cache warmup window up to 14 days.
- Light = async feedback only (~1 form every 2 weeks), ops SLA 5 days.
- Feature asks: logged as RFCs; only triaged, not committed. If partner funds dev, we can create a scoped change order.

Ethan (Eng): technical note: enabling KV warmup requires a short-lived namespace. We need a teardown hook after window expires. Also add rate-limits so warm caches don't blow memory.

Zoe (CS): replacement rule: if partner misses two scheduled milestone checkpoints without rescheduling, mark as "no-show" and release slot to waitlist. pilot-bot should send an auto-probation notice first.

pilot-bot: probation workflow configured: send notice at missed-checkpoint -> 72h to respond -> if no response mark slot released and invite top waitlist candidate with 48h acceptance window.

Felipe (Design): Add an upfront "time commitment badge" in invites: Deep="~3h/week", Light="~1h/2w". Also show expected artifacts: smoke-test pass, recorded kickoff, baseline survey.

Rina (Legal): privacy note: if partner is in regulated industry, mark as "high compliance"; require security contact and longer onboarding. We'll need a short questionnaire to flag this on recruitment.

Tara (PM): recruitment scoring (quick): production-usage(40), technical-contact(20), compliance-risk(-20 if regulated), strategic-fit(20), willingness-to-schedule(20). We can threshold >=70 for deep.

Ethan (Eng): monitoring: tag all pilot traffic with pilot_slot_id and partner_id. We should also export a small debug bundle (logs + traces) for deep partners only and auto-retire bundles older than 30d.

Zoe (CS): incentive split suggestion: Deep = $1k credit + product roadmap sync once per quarter; Light = $300 credit. Add a small "on-time feedback" bonus: $200 if partner completes all required feedback on schedule in first month.

Felipe (Design): measurement: collect partner sentiment (scale -2..+2), feedback completion rate, and number of actionable items (ownerable within 2 sprints). Display these on the pilot dashboard per slot.

Rina (Legal): escalation for regressions: if pilot causes a regression impacting other customers, team will execute rollback; partner slot may be paused pending root-cause. Add clause: we reserve right to rollback/disable partner-specific config to protect production.

Tara (PM): acceptance criteria to move partner from "onboarding" to "active": passed smoke test, signed pilot addendum (if telemetry enabled), kickoff recorded, baseline survey submitted. Product-level launch criteria for the program: avg feedback >=6/10 and at least 4 actionable items surfaced in first 30 days.

Ethan (Eng): one more operational ask: timezone distribution. We should cap deep partners to max 2 partners in overlapping engineer-intensive timezones to avoid burnout. Add scheduling constraint in spreadsheet.

Zoe (CS): I'll add that column. Also adding recruitment email draft: "Short: invited to pilot Redwood inference features. Expect ~3h/week for deep (ops + calls). Incentive: $1k credit + early roadmap visibility. Can you commit? Provide POC & timezone."

Felipe (Design): UX small ask: add a single checkbox in the invite for telemetry opt-in so we can track consent.

Rina (Legal): also require partner to confirm they own data they're sharing (simple checkbox); put link to pilot addendum.

Tara (PM): thanks. I'll consolidate into a one-pager and recruitment sheet and post to the pilot playbook. Quick thumbs?

Ethan (Eng): :thumbsup:

Zoe (CS): :thumbsup:

Felipe (Design): :thumbsup:

Rina (Legal): :thumbsup:

Tara (PM): perfect. I'll push invites 09:00 PT tomorrow and wire pilot-bot to the spreadsheet. If anything blocks overnight ping me.
